styles.name: golden-spiral
styles.description: Fibonacci-square tiling with quarter-circle arcs forming the golden logarithmic spiral; squares and arcs revealed one step per eased progress

styles.name: golden-rectangle
styles.description: Recursive φ-rectangle subdivision into a square + smaller φ-rectangle — the whirling-rectangles diagram, with each subdivision revealed as progress rises

styles.name: fibonacci-squares
styles.description: Outward Fibonacci-square tiling (1,1,2,3,5,8,13,21,34…): each square outline appears as progress advances, building the canonical φ-rectangle mosaic

styles.name: pentagram
styles.description: Nested pentagram-in-pentagon: each star's inner pentagon contains a smaller pentagram scaled by 1/φ², revealing infinite φ self-similarity as progress deepens

styles.name: pentagon-nest
styles.description: Concentric pentagons each scaled 1/φ² smaller, counter-rotating with time — a hypnotic tunnel of five-fold symmetry

styles.name: golden-gnomon
styles.description: 36-72-72 golden gnomon recursively bisected into smaller golden triangles — the geometric basis of Penrose tilings, depth revealed with progress

styles.name: phi-phyllotaxis-pent
styles.description: Five-fold phyllotaxis: seeds placed at the golden angle but grouped into five symmetric spiral arms, creating pentagonal lattice symmetry with φ spacing

styles.name: nautilus
styles.description: φ-logarithmic nautilus spiral r=a·φ^(θ·2/π) with chambered septa every quarter turn — the classic cephalopod shell built from pure golden-ratio growth

styles.name: golden-angle-rays
styles.description: Rays at successive 137.5° golden-angle increments from the center, each growing longer — the irrational spacing that prevents clustering and produces optimal coverage of the disk

styles.name: dodecagram
styles.description: Dodecagram {12/5}: connecting every 5th vertex of a regular 12-gon produces a twelve-pointed φ-star; chords materialise progressively while the star rotates

styles.name: kepler-triangle
styles.description: Kepler triangle fan: right triangles with sides 1:√φ:φ tiled around the center, each rotated by the golden angle — where Pythagoras meets φ
